Join two data frames using a Bloom filter pre-filter

Source: R/bloomjoin.R
bloom_join.Rd

Join two data frames using a Bloom filter pre-filter

Usage

bloom_join(
  x,
  y,
  by = NULL,
  type = c("inner", "left", "right", "full", "semi", "anti"),
  engine = c("auto", "bloom", "fuse"),
  prefilter_side = c("auto", "x", "y"),
  fpr = 0.01,
  n_hint = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x, y

Data frames to join.

by

A character vector or named character vector specifying the join columns, just like the by argument in the dplyr join verbs.

type

Type of join to perform. One of "inner", "left", "right", "full", "semi", or "anti".

engine

Probabilistic pre-filter to use. Currently only "bloom" is implemented; "auto" resolves to "bloom" and "fuse" is reserved for a future binary-fuse implementation.

prefilter_side

Which input to pre-filter. "x" filters the first table, "y" filters the second table, and "auto" picks a side based on join semantics and distinct-count estimates.

fpr

Target false positive rate for the Bloom filter. Must be between 0 and 1.

n_hint

Optional estimated distinct counts for the join keys. Supply a numeric scalar to use the same hint for both tables or a named list/vector with entries x and/or y.

verbose

Logical flag controlling diagnostic output.

Value

A data frame identical to the corresponding dplyr join with an additional "bloomjoin" class and a bloom_metadata attribute describing the pre-filter decision.

Examples

x <- data.frame(id = 1:100000, value_x = rnorm(100000))
y <- data.frame(id = 50001:60000, value_y = rnorm(10000))
bloom_join(x, y, by = "id", verbose = TRUE)
